bank.blurb: Raises the nation’s gold storage by 1000 (it starts at 2000).
bank.name: Bank

forge.blurb: Unlocks Military research and adds 2 Military points every 10 s. Upgrades to a Battle Forge, then a War Forge.
forge.name: Forge

granary.blurb: Raises the nation’s food storage by 1000 (it starts at 2000).
granary.name: Granary

magetower.blurb: Unlocks Magic research and adds 2 Magic points every 10 s. Upgrades to a Mage Sanctum, then a Mage Arcanum.
magetower.name: Mage Tower

market.blurb: A small, steady gold income; can be built in any province.
market.name: Marketplace

pyre.blurb: Raised by a Warlock on a free building plot. Burns 10 wood every 10 s for 20 gold. Build it up into a Grand Pyre: 20 wood for 50 gold. One per living Warlock.
pyre.name: Sacred Pyre

storehouse.blurb: Raises the nation’s wood storage by 1000 (it starts at 2000).
storehouse.name: Storehouse

temple.blurb: A marble temple: adds 2 Government research points every payout. No research needed to build it; it never upgrades.
temple.name: Temple

abandon: Costs 1000 gold to begin. When finished, your school and all of its spells are forgotten, and you can choose a new school.
apprentice: Your Mage limit rises by 1: you can train a second Mage.
arboreal: A Mage can close a forest path again with 10 seconds of casting (200 mana).
arcanum: Lets a Mage Sanctum be upgraded to a Mage Arcanum (Magic Tier III).
arcscouts: Every Mage Tower (and its upgrades) sees all neighboring provinces, permanently.
arcvision: Mage Towers reveal stealthed units within their sight.
armyofdeath: Risen Dead raises 10 soldiers in a battle.
arrowslits: Forts and capitals shoot at enemy armies standing in their province: one volley every 10 s, enough to bring down a Footman. An occupied fort stops shooting.
autobuild: Tier III+: offered once every other Tier III Government technology is done. Masons can be set to build one kind of building on their own, in every province that has room, whenever you can afford it.
autoscout: Idle Wayfinders survey explored, unsurveyed provinces on their own. Toggle it on a Wayfinder’s command card.
bank: Unlocks the Bank: +1000 gold storage each (the nation starts able to hold 2000).
battleforge: Lets a Forge be upgraded to a Battle Forge (Military Tier II). Offered once two Tier I Military technologies are researched.
bountiful: Harvest makes Farms give 20% more food.
bridges: Masons can build a bridge across a river border (200 wood, 150 gold, 90 s). It takes no building plot, and only one of the two provinces has to be yours. Needs Stone Walls, Moat, the Forge and Refined Lumber Mills.
charon: Grave Robbing gives 3 gold for every point of mana.
clearthoughts: A 3-second cast (50 mana): every army within 3 provinces of the Mage is revealed for 20 seconds. 40-second cooldown.
commune: Opening a forest path takes 10 seconds.
crypticwand: Mages can carry a Cryptic Wand: attack 3 (Wand 2), leaving a hand free for a shield. Every spell costs 10% less mana while they carry it.
curse1: Autocast (50 mana): when an army with a Mage starts a battle, its weapons deal +5% damage. 5-minute cooldown per army.
curse2: Cursed Weapons deal +10% damage; cooldown 3 minutes.
curse3: Cursed Weapons deal +15% damage; cooldown 90 seconds.
deathtax: Grave Robbing gives 2 gold for every point of mana.
dualwield: Berserkers and Ogres with a one-handed weapon can carry a second one in the off hand (set it in the Armory). The off-hand weapon hits for half its attack.
earthquake: A Mage standing in an enemy province your army occupies can cast an Earthquake (200 mana: it needs Magic Abundance): after 30 seconds every building in that province is destroyed, and every wall on its borders takes 120 wall damage (enough to bring down any wall).
effadmin: Every Fort (and your capital) allows 2 more provinces: 6 outposts each instead of 4.
enigmaticwand: Mages can carry an Enigmatic Wand: attack 5, with a shield. Every spell costs 20% less mana while they carry it.
eyesforest: A Mage looks through a border of trees beside him (3 seconds of casting, 25 mana): both provinces on either side of it are in sight for 1 minute.
farsight: Wayfinders see into every province next to the one they stand in, and every unexplored province they look into is explored for good.
fiery1: Autocast (50 mana, no cooldown): when an army with a Warlock starts a battle, every blow has a 5% chance to strike twice as hard.
fiery2: Fiery Weapons: a 10% chance of a double blow.
fiery3: Fiery Weapons: a 15% chance of a double blow.
firetrap: A Warlock buries a fire trap in his province (3 seconds of casting, 50 mana). The next enemy army to enter any part of that province is engulfed: 150 damage that ignores armor, to its front line. One trap per Warlock.
forest: A Mage standing in a province you own or occupy can open a path through a border of trees after 20 seconds of casting (200 mana). Lumber Mills are unaffected.
forestspirit: A Druid channels a Forest Spirit into the province he stands in: while he keeps it up, the province makes twice the gold, wood, food and research. It drains 1 mana a second, and he regains none meanwhile.
forge: Unlocks the Forge, which opens Military research. Owning a Barracks makes this technology 50% more likely to be offered.
forts: Raises the Fort limit from 1 to 3.
forts2: Raises the Fort limit from 3 to 5.
forts3: Raises the Fort limit from 5 to 7.
gelemental: A Druid summons a towering man of living water for 2 minutes (3 seconds of casting, 100 mana): 500 health, no armor, 50 damage a swing. He joins the Druid’s army (or forms one), fights, and can capture provinces. 5-minute cooldown per Druid.
granary: Unlocks the Granary: +1000 food storage each (the nation starts able to hold 2000).
grandstave: Mages can carry a Grand Stave: attack 6 (Stave 4), and every spell casts 10% faster while they carry it.
graverob: A 3-second cast that spends all of the Mage’s mana: 1 gold for every point. Then the nation waits 3 minutes.
hallways: Opening a mountain tunnel takes 10 seconds.
harvest: A Mage channels it for as long as he stands still: every Farm you own gives 10% more food. It drains 1 mana a second, and he regains none while channeling. One Mage casts it at a time.
haunt: A Mage haunts the province he stands in (25 mana, no cooldown): you keep seeing it for 1 minute, even after he leaves.
horde: An army of 10 or more cavalry and no other units has 1.3 times the health. A horseshoe over the army shows when it is active.
horse-breeding: Needs Building: Stable (Government). Cavalry can ride Arabians (fastest, fragile) or Mongolian horses (cheap to feed, at home in forest and swamp, weak charge).
horse-training: Unlocks Friesians (the hardest charge) and armored Percherons (toughest, but slow and hungry).
magetower: Unlocks the Mage Tower, which trains Mages and opens Magic research. Your first tower lets you choose a school of magic.
magicabund: Your Magic Users can hold up to 200 mana.
magicwell: Your Magic Users can hold up to 150 mana (100 before).
magnificent: Harvest makes Farms give 30% more food.
market: Unlocks the Marketplace: +3 gold every payout, buildable in any province.
mending: A Mage heals an army’s wounds back to full over 1 minute. 25 mana, no cooldown.
mindread: Clear Thoughts reveals every army on the map.
moat: Your forts and capital are ringed with water: an enemy needs 10 seconds longer to capture them.
mushroom: Farms can be built in swamps too: damp, dark beds of mushrooms.
mythicstave: Mages can carry a Mythic Stave: attack 9, and every spell casts 20% faster while they carry it.
necro: Risen Dead raises 7 soldiers in a battle.
pathfire: A Warlock fires up his army (50 mana): 100% faster for 10 seconds. 1-minute cooldown per Warlock.
pathflame: Path of Fire: 125% faster for 15 seconds.
pathinferno: Path of Fire: 150% faster for 20 seconds.
planar: Trading gives 1 of each resource for every point of mana.
refmills: Every Lumber Mill gives another +1 wood.
refmines: Every Gold Mine gives another +2 gold.
retained: Every research tree (Government, Military and Magic) offers one more technology to choose from (4 instead of 3).
retained2: Every research tree (Government, Military and Magic) offers one more technology again (5 to choose from).
rift: Pick any explored province you may enter (your land, unclaimed land, or a nation you are at war or in a truce with): after 3 seconds of casting (100 mana) the Mage and his army are carried there. 2-minute cooldown for the nation.
risen: Autocast: the first time a soldier of the army falls in a battle, the Mage spends 50 mana and the dead rise: that soldier and the next 4 to fall get straight back up, looking rather worse for it (same strength). Then it stops; when the battle ends it has a 2-minute cooldown. One Mage keeps this or Cursed Weapons ready, not both.
roads: Masons can build a dirt road across an open border (75 wood, 25 gold). Units move 25% faster along it.
roads2: Every road is relaid in gravel: units move 35% faster along roads.
roads3: Every road is paved with cobbles: units move 50% faster along roads.
rockarmor: Autocast (50 mana, no cooldown): when an army with a Druid starts a battle, plates of stone gather round it: a shield worth 10% of the army’s total health soaks up the damage before any soldier is hurt.
s-kite: Kite Shield for one-handed designs: +6 armor.
s-round: Round Shield for one-handed designs: +3 armor.
s-tower: Tower Shield for one-handed designs: +10 armor, but 8% slower.
sacredpyre: A Warlock standing in one of your provinces raises a Sacred Pyre there (3 seconds of casting, 100 mana and 200 wood). For 1 minute that province makes 110 more gold every 10 s. Then the nation waits 3 minutes.
sanctum: Lets a Mage Tower be upgraded to a Mage Sanctum (Magic Tier II).
school-arcane: Commit to Arcane magic: far sight from towers, mind reading, trading across worlds, traps and rifts.
school-death: Commit to Necromancy: cursed weapons, mountain passages, the risen dead and grave riches.
school-elemental: Commit to Elemental magic: rock armor, whispering rocks, forest spirits, town portals and a grand elemental of living water.
school-life: Commit to Herbomancy: harvests, protective skins, healing and the forest.
school-pyro: Commit to Pyromancy: fiery weapons, scouting pyres, fire traps, sacred pyres and paths of fire.
scoutpyre: A Warlock lights a pyre where he stands (3 seconds of casting, 25 mana). For 1 minute it sees every neighboring province in its line of sight. 1-minute cooldown per Warlock.
scoutsight: Your scouts (Wayfinders, Scouts, Swampstriders) learn Scout Sight: after 5 seconds of focus a scout detects every unit in his field of vision, sneaking ones too, for as long as he holds still. He can’t move or sneak meanwhile: ordering him to move ends it.
sealed: A Mage can seal a mountain tunnel again with 10 seconds of casting (200 mana).
skin: Autocast (50 mana, no cooldown): when an army with a Mage starts a battle, its soldiers get +5% health.
skull-cracked: Warlocks with a wand can hold a Cracked Skull in the off hand: +1 attack, and the Fireball casts 2 s faster. Set it in the Armory.
skull-flawless: Warlocks with a wand can hold a Flawless Skull in the off hand: +3 attack, and the Fireball casts 6 s faster.
skull-polished: Warlocks with a wand can hold a Polished Skull in the off hand: +2 attack, and the Fireball casts 4 s faster.
sophmills: Every Lumber Mill gives another +1 wood.
sophmines: Every Gold Mine gives another +2 gold.
stable: Unlocks the Stable, which lets a Barracks in the same province train Cavalry.
stasis: A Mage sets a trap in his province (3 seconds of casting, 50 mana); the next enemy army there can’t leave for 10 seconds (it can still fight). One trap at a time; no cooldown.
stealth: Wayfinders can sneak: three times slower, but enemy armies can’t see them. Without it, an enemy army that finds a Wayfinder kills him.
stockmarket: Trading gives 2 of each resource for every 3 points of mana.
storehouse: Unlocks the Storehouse: +1000 wood storage each (the nation starts able to hold 2000).
terrascape: A Mage grows a line of trees along an open border, with a forest path left open in the middle: only a path through the trees remains. 5 minutes of casting, 100 mana.
thugs2: Every Thug Den holds one more Thug (3 instead of 2).
thugs3: Every Thug Den holds one more Thug again (4).
townportal: After 3 seconds of casting (100 mana), a Druid and the army he is in are carried to your capital. 5-minute cooldown per Druid.
traderoutes: Your capital makes +1 gold for every Marketplace it can reach by road, through any number of your provinces.
trading: A 3-second cast that spends all of the Mage’s mana: 1 food, 1 gold and 1 wood for every 3 points. Then the nation waits 3 minutes.
twohand: Protectors can be designed to fight two-handed (set the grip in the Armory): every other round they deal nothing, and the next a blow 2.5 times as hard, 125% of their damage over time. Champions fight this way without it.
underworld: A Mage standing in a province you own or occupy can open a tunnel through a mountain border after 20 seconds of casting (200 mana).
w-bastard: Bastard Sword for the Armory: attack 10, one-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.
w-battleaxe: Battle Axe for the Armory: attack 14, one-handed. Critical strike: each blow has a 10% chance to do double damage.
w-bearded: Bearded Axe for the Armory: attack 10, one-handed. Critical strike: each blow has a 10% chance to do double damage.
w-braidedsling: Your Slingers trade the Wool Sling for the Braided Sling: attack 9 (from 6). Every Slinger you have is re-armed at once, in the field too.
w-compositebow: Your Archers trade the Short Bow for the Composite Bow: attack 9 (from 6). Every Archer you have is re-armed at once, in the field too.
w-estoc: Estoc for the Armory: attack 20, one-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.
w-gladius: Gladius for the Armory: attack 10, one-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.
w-greatsword: Great Sword for the Armory: attack 30, two-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.
w-halberd: Halberd for the Armory: attack 18, two-handed. +50% damage against cavalry.
w-leathersling: Your Slingers trade the Braided Sling for the Leather Sling: attack 12 (from 9). Every Slinger you have is re-armed at once, in the field too.
w-levercrossbow: Your Crossbowmen trade the Hand-drawn Crossbow for the Lever Crossbow: attack 9 (from 6). Every Crossbowman you have is re-armed at once, in the field too.
w-longbow: Your Archers trade the Composite Bow for the Long Bow: attack 12 (from 9). Every Archer you have is re-armed at once, in the field too.
w-longsword: Long Sword for the Armory: attack 14, one-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.
w-mace: Mace for the Armory: attack 8, one-handed. Crushing: ignores half of enemy armor, and deals 150% damage to soldiers in plate.
w-morningstar: Morning Star for the Armory: attack 11, one-handed. Crushing: ignores half of enemy armor, and deals 150% damage to soldiers in plate.
w-pike: Pike for the Armory: attack 9, two-handed. +50% damage against cavalry.
w-polearm: Polearm for the Armory: attack 13, two-handed. +50% damage against cavalry.
w-rapier: Rapier for the Armory: attack 14, one-handed. Parry: take 10% less damage.
w-waraxe: War Axe for the Armory: attack 20, one-handed. Critical strike: each blow has a 10% chance to do double damage.
w-warhammer: War Hammer for the Armory: attack 15, one-handed. Crushing: ignores half of enemy armor, and deals 150% damage to soldiers in plate.
w-windlass: Your Crossbowmen trade the Lever Crossbow for the Windlass Crossbow: attack 12 (from 9). Every Crossbowman you have is re-armed at once, in the field too.
walls: Masons can close an open border with a wooden palisade (150 wood, 100 gold). Every wall has a gate that only its owner’s units can pass. Forts raise walls with gates on all their open borders.
walls2: Walls are built of stone, and existing palisades are rebuilt in stone: three times as strong.
warforge: Lets a Battle Forge be upgraded to a War Forge (Military Tier III).
wrocks: A Druid raises whispering stones on a mountain border of the province he stands in (3 seconds of casting, 25 mana): both provinces on either side are in sight for 1 minute.

gov.rate: Forts +2, Capital +3, Temples +2 per payout (outposts give none)

mag.locked: Research the Mage Tower (Government Tier II), then build one to unlock Magic.
mag.rate: Mage Tower +2, Sanctum +4, Arcanum +6 per payout

mil.locked: Research the Forge (Government Tier I), then build one to unlock Military research.
mil.rate: Forge +2, Battle Forge +4, War Forge +6 per payout

mage:A.blurb: Casts the spells of your school. Joins an army to fight in it and power its battle spells.
mage:A.name: Mage

barracks.note: trains Protectors (and Champions with a Hall of Champions)

farm.blurb: An apple orchard: +5 food every payout.

magetower.blurb: A great tree whose canopy grows with every upgrade. Trains Druids, unlocks Magic research and adds 2 Magic points every payout. Upgrades to a Majestic Grove, then a Magnificent Grove.
magetower.name: Grove

market.blurb: A bustling forest bazaar: +3 gold every payout. With Community, +1 more for each other building in its province.
market.name: Bazaar

stable.blurb: A longhouse hung with antlers, where Champions are sworn. Lets a Barracks in the same province train Champions.
stable.name: Hall of Champions

storehouse.blurb: Built inside a hollow giant fallen tree: +1000 wood storage.

temple.blurb: A statue of a veiled woman, praying humbly: adds 2 Government research points every payout.
temple.name: Shrine

rep-sword: Thrusting Sword soldiers deal 5% more damage.

horse-breeding: Needs Building: Hall of Champions (Government). Champions can wield the Ancient Hammer (crushing, tougher, slower) or the Wrathful Spear (quicker on the march).
horse-training: Unlocks the Worldbreaker Axe (critical strikes) and the Oblivion Blade (the deadliest and toughest Champion weapon, but the slowest and dearest).
stable: Unlocks the Hall of Champions, which lets a Barracks train Champions.
traderoutes: Every Bazaar makes 1 more gold per payout for each other building in its province (a Bazaar in a province with 5 other buildings: +5 gold).

mage:A: Casts the spells of your school. Joins an army to fight in it and power its battle spells.
pioneer:B: Explores and surveys land, and slips through borders of trees.
